content: The estrogen patch is a transdermal delivery system designed to administer estradiol, a form of estrogen. It is primarily used as part of hormone replacement therapy (HRT) to address menopausal symptoms such as hot flashes and vaginal dryness, as well as to prevent osteoporosis. Unlike oral estrogen tablets, the estrogen patch delivers the hormone through the skin, bypassing the liver. This method avoids the hepatic first-pass metabolism associated with oral medications and results in slightly different effects on triglycerides and cholesterol levels compared to oral estrogens. The patch is applied to areas of fatty tissue on the skin, with the preferred sites being the lower abdomen or buttocks. It should never be applied to the breasts. Depending on the specific brand, the patch is typically replaced either twice weekly or weekly. Several brand names of estrogen patches are available, including: Alora® (United States) Climara® (United States) Dermestril® (United Kingdom) Elleste Solo® (United States) Esclim® (United States) Estraderm® (United Kingdom) Estradot® (United Kingdom) Evorel® (United Kingdom) Fematrix® (United Kingdom) Fempatch® (United States) FemSeven® (United Kingdom) Menostar® (United States) Vivelle-Dot® (United States) The Vivelle-Dot® patch was originally marketed as Vivelle® by Novartis. However, in 2000, a smaller version with improved adhesion was introduced, replacing the original Vivelle®. As a result, Vivelle® was discontinued in 2003.
